---
url: /myco/tutorials/first-item.md
---
# Your first item

A guided walk through one task's lifecycle: scaffold a ledger,
create a task, move it through the state machine, and close it —
seeing the markdown change under you each step.

You'll need `myco` installed (see
[getting started](../getting-started.md)) and a git repo to play
in:

```sh
mkdir ledger-demo && cd ledger-demo
git init && git commit --allow-empty -m init
```

## 1. Scaffold the ledger

```sh
myco init
```

This creates a `project/` directory — actually a git worktree of
the new orphan `project` branch — seeded with `TODO.md`,
`BACKLOG.md`, `index.md`, `meta.toml`, and empty item dirs.
`git worktree list` shows it; `.gitignore` hides it from your
code branch.

## 2. Add a task

```sh
myco todo add "write the tutorial" --pri high --label docs
```

```text
added T-001 open pri:high #docs write the tutorial
```

myco allocated `T-001` (the `t` counter in `meta.toml`) and
appended one line to `project/TODO.md`:

```markdown
- [ ] T-001 write the tutorial · pri:high · created:2026-10-29 · #docs
```

Everything after the title is `·`-separated tokens —
`pri:`, `owner:`, `#label`, `blocks:`, `epic:`, `ms:`.

Nest a sub-task under it:

```sh
myco todo add "review it" --parent T-001
```

Children are `- [ ]` lines indented two spaces under the parent.
They are full items — same metadata, same state machine — and
`done`/`defer` on a parent act on the whole subtree.

## 3. Move it through the state machine

```sh
myco item set T-001 --status in-progress --owner devin
myco board
```

```text
+---------+-----------------+---------+--------------------------+---------+
| Backlog | Open            | Claimed | In Progress              | Blocked |
+---------+-----------------+---------+--------------------------+---------+
|         | T-002 review it |         | T-001 write the tutorial |         |
+---------+-----------------+---------+--------------------------+---------+
```

Statuses are `open → claimed → in-progress → done`, with
`blocked` and `deferred` off the main path — see
[the file spec](../explanation/file-spec.md#state-machine) for
the legal transitions. `item set` walks the machine one step at a
time; an illegal jump errors and tells you the valid targets.

Park something instead of finishing it:

```sh
myco todo defer T-002   # → deferred; the line moves to BACKLOG.md
myco backlog promote T-002   # → open; back to TODO.md
```

## 4. Leave a handoff

```sh
myco handoff T-001 --note "Done: draft. Next: screenshots." --actor devin
myco resume T-001
```

`handoff` appends a dated entry to `handoffs/T-001.md`;
`resume` prints the minimal restart context — the item, its
`blocks:` deps, latest handoffs, open checklist.

## 5. Finish and check

```sh
myco todo done T-001
myco check
```

```text
check: clean
```

Done tasks are *removed* from `TODO.md` — the `project` branch
history is the record. Every verb you ran was one atomic commit
on that branch (`git -C project log --oneline` shows them all).

## Recap

| you ran | myco did |
|---|---|
| `todo add` | alloc id, append line to `TODO.md` |
| `item set --status` | one legal state-machine step |
| `todo defer` / `backlog promote` | move the line TODO ↔ BACKLOG |
| `handoff` / `resume` | append-only session notes / restart context |
| `todo done` | `done`, then delete the line |
| `check` | validate files, state machine, index drift |

Every write went through a verb — hand-editing works too (the
markdown is canonical), but `myco check` is the referee either
way.

Next: [the daily agent loop](../how-to/agent-loop.md) for how an
agent drives these verbs, or the
[CLI reference](../reference/cli.md) for the full surface.

# Set up myco on a repository

`myco init` turns any git repo into a myco project: an orphan
`project` branch checked out as a `project/` worktree.

```sh
cd your-repo
myco init
```

## What it creates

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `project/` | git worktree on the orphan `project` branch |
| `project/meta.toml` | repo name + per-kind id counters (`[next]`) |
| `project/TODO.md` | active tasks |
| `project/BACKLOG.md` | deferred items |
| `project/index.md` | human-readable ledger index |
| `project/issues/`, `proposals/`, `plans/`, `adrs/`, `handoffs/` | file-backed item dirs |
| `.gitignore` += `project/` | keeps the worktree out of code commits |

`init` commits the scaffold on the `project` branch — your code
branch only gains the `.gitignore` line.

## Re-running init

`init` is idempotent: a valid existing worktree gets its scaffold
verified/repaired instead of re-created. It is the safe "is this
repo set up?" probe.

## Overrides and discovery

`--root` picks the repo, `--dir` picks a non-default worktree
path (init uses it instead of `<root>/project`):

```sh
myco init --root ~/GitHub/9aia/sepia
myco init --dir ~/work/ledger          # worktree somewhere else
```

Every other verb discovers the project the same way, in order:

1. `--dir` — explicit worktree path
2. `--root` — repo root (worktree is `<root>/project`)
3. `project_dir` in `myco.toml` (see [config](../reference/config.md))
4. walk up from cwd for a `project/` worktree on branch `project`
5. cwd inside the worktree itself

A non-standard worktree location stays discoverable if you set
`project_dir` (relative to the repo root) in a `myco.toml` —
the search order is `$MYCO_CONFIG` → `./myco.toml` (where you
run `myco`) → `~/.config/myco/myco.toml`.

## If the repo has a `pm/` dir

Don't `init` — run [`myco migrate`](migrate.md) instead. It
converts the legacy `pm/` layout into a fresh `project/` worktree
in one pass.

# Run the daily agent loop

The core loop for an agent (or a human driving like one):
orient → claim → work → hand off → resume. Every step is a verb;
`--json` on all of them.

## Orient

```sh
myco status --prompt    # token-sized digest, sized for a context window
```

`status --prompt` is the session opener: counts by kind, what's
in progress, what's open — enough to pick work without reading
the files. `myco status` (no flag) is the human-readable version;
`myco board` and `myco report` give the kanban and the trend.

## Claim

```sh
myco item set T-012 --status claimed --owner devin
myco item set T-012 --status in-progress
```

`claimed` says "an actor owns this" before work starts;
`in-progress` says "being worked now". Both are single legal
steps from `open`. Owner ids are namespaced actor strings —
`devin`, `human:luis`, … — so multiple agents can share a ledger.

Hit a wall mid-task: `myco item set T-012 --status blocked`.
Need the details: `myco item show T-012` (add `--json` for the
full item + location + body).

## Hand off

Before the session ends, leave resumable state on the item:

```sh
myco handoff T-012 --actor devin --session cli:$$ \
  --note "Done: parser landed. Next: emitter. Open: archive semantics."
```

`--note -` reads stdin — pipe a generated summary. See
[handoffs](handoff.md) for the full verb behavior.

## Resume

Next session — human or agent — pulls the restart context:

```sh
myco resume T-012          # compact prompt-ready block
myco resume T-012 --json   # {item, location, blocks_titles, handoffs, open_checklist}
```

Then `myco status --prompt` for the ledger-wide picture and the
loop restarts.

## Hygiene

```sh
myco check          # exits 1 with findings
myco check --fix    # safe repairs + one commit
```

Run `check` when files were hand-edited or the index may have
drifted — it validates the [file spec](../explanation/file-spec.md),
state machine, and index snapshots.

## No-commit mode

Batch or scripted flows can skip the per-verb commit with
`--no-commit` or `MYCO_NO_COMMIT=1`, then commit once:

```sh
myco commit -m "chore: end-of-day ledger tidy"
```

`myco commit` stages all worktree changes and commits with a
conventional message (default `chore: update project ledger`).

---

---
url: /myco/how-to/handoff.md
---
# Hand off work between sessions

Attach resumable state to any item at the end of a working
session, then pull the minimal context to restart it later.

```sh
myco handoff T-012 --note "parser done, emitter next" --actor devin --session cli:abc123
myco resume T-012   # minimal context block to restart work
```

## `myco handoff <id>`

Appends a dated entry to `handoffs/<ID>.md` — works on every item
kind (`T-`, `I-`, `P-`, `ADR-`, `PL-`), live or archived. The item
must exist; the note is required.

* `--note "…"` — the handoff text (done/next/open). `-` reads stdin.
* `--actor <id>` — who wrote it (`devin`, `human:luis`; default `cli`).
* `--session <id>` — provenance, any id string (a sepia session id,
  `cli:<pid>`, …). Recorded verbatim, never interpreted.

Each call is one appended `##` entry and one commit
(`chore: handoff <id>`). Files are append-only — history inside a
file is never rewritten.

## `myco resume <id> [--last N]`

Emits the restart context as a compact prompt block:

```text
I-003 in-progress pri:high owner:devin #index memory leak
in: issues/issue-0003-memory-leak.md
blocks:
  T-010 store layer
handoffs:
2026-10-29 · devin · session:cli:abc123
  Done: repro. Next: fix.
open checklist:
  - [ ] add regression test
```

`--json` gives `{item, location, blocks_titles, handoffs[],
open_checklist}` — the same data for machines. `--last N` shows
only the latest N handoff entries (default 10).

`myco item show <id>` surfaces a `handoffs: N` count; `myco check`
keeps `handoffs/` honest — files for removed items are archived to
`handoffs/archive/` by `--fix`, and malformed entries are parse
findings.

For the sepia-side wiring (session hooks calling these verbs), see
[session continuity with sepia](session-continuity.md).

---

---
url: /myco/how-to/session-continuity.md
---
# Session continuity with sepia

sepia owns session lifecycle; myco owns work memory. The boundary
is two verbs — no sepia code lives in this repo, and no myco code
in sepia. Each side just calls the other's CLI.

## The pattern

Session end (sepia hook) — leave a resumable note on the item you
were working, tagged with the sepia session id:

```sh
myco handoff T-012 \
  --actor devin \
  --session <sepia-session-id> \
  --note "Done: store layer landed. Next: wire verbs. Open: archive semantics for ADRs."
```

`--note -` reads stdin, so a hook can pipe a generated summary.
`--session` accepts any id string — a sepia session id, a
`cli:<pid>:<ts>` fallback, whatever wrote the entry. It's
provenance only; myco records it and never interprets it.

Session start — pull the minimal restart context into the prompt:

```sh
myco resume T-012 --json
```

`resume` returns the item (status, priority, owner, labels), the
titles of its `blocks:` dependencies, the latest handoff entries,
and the unchecked `- [ ]` checklist items for file-backed items —
the single-item counterpart of `myco status --prompt`. Human
output is a compact prompt-ready block; `--last N` caps the
entries shown (default 10).

## Where handoffs live

`handoffs/<ID>.md` — one append-only file per item, uniform across
every kind:

```markdown
+++
item = "T-012"
+++

# Handoffs — T-012

## 2026-10-29 · devin · session:cli:abc123
Done: store layer landed. Next: wire verbs. Open: archive semantics for ADRs.
```

Entries are never rewritten — each `myco handoff` is one appended
`## <date> · <actor> · session:<id>` heading and one atomic commit
(`chore: handoff T-012`) on the `project` branch, so the branch
history is the audit trail.

When an item is removed — done tasks leave `TODO.md` — its
handoff file becomes orphaned. `myco check` reports it and
`myco check --fix` moves it to `handoffs/archive/`: the live dir
stays clean, the knowledge survives, and `myco resume` on an
archived item still finds it.

url: /myco/how-to/migrate.md
---
# Migrate a legacy ledger

`myco migrate` brings pre-v2 ledgers up to the current spec.
Two modes, auto-detected by what's on disk.

## `pm/` → `project/`

A `pm/` directory at the repo root is the pre-worktree layout.
One command converts and removes it:

```sh
cd your-repo
myco migrate
```

* `pm/TODO.md` / `pm/BACKLOG.md` bullets become `T-` items in the
  new `TODO.md` / `BACKLOG.md` — done items are dropped
* `pm/ROADMAP.md` becomes a `plans/` file
* any other `pm/*.md` becomes an `issues/` file
* a fresh `project/` worktree is scaffolded (the `init` path)
* `pm/` is removed and its deletion committed on the code branch

## Legacy `project/` → v2

Files already on a `project` branch are normalized in place:

* id-less items get ids
* `[x]`/done items drop (history keeps them)
* heading-like lines become `##` sections
* frontmatter-less files in item dirs are *adopted* — the
  filename's number is honored when free (`0001-foo.md` →
  `ADR-0001`); collisions take the next unclaimed number with a
  warning. Adopted files get synthesized frontmatter and the
  canonical name
* everything is re-emitted canonically

## After migrating

```sh
myco check        # should report clean
myco status       # the ledger, v2-shaped
```

`--json` on `migrate` returns the run's counters — items
converted, ids allocated, files moved, warnings. If the run left
unparsed lines, they're listed there; fix by hand and `check`
again.

url: /myco/how-to/import-work.md
---
# Import external work

`myco absorb` pulls work that lives elsewhere into the ledger —
code comments, Jira exports, GitHub issue dumps.

## Sweep code comments

```sh
myco absorb comments                  # the repo root
myco absorb comments --path src/ --kinds TODO,FIXME,HACK
myco absorb comments --to issues      # file issues instead of backlog items
myco absorb comments --dry            # report without creating
```

Uses ripgrep (`rg` must be installed), respects `.gitignore`, and
skips `project/`, `docs/`, `target/`. Findings land as `T-` items
— `BACKLOG.md` by default, `issues/` files with `--to issues`.

## Jira CSV

```sh
myco absorb jira export.csv
myco absorb jira export.csv --include-done
```

`Done`/`Resolved` rows are skipped unless `--include-done` — then
they're created `done` and archived.

## GitHub issue dump

```sh
myco absorb github dump.json          # or dump.csv
myco absorb github dump.json --include-done
```

JSON input is an array of issue objects — a
`gh issue list --json number,title,state,labels,assignees,body`
dump works as-is (`labels` entries can be `"name"` strings or
`{name:…}` objects, `assignee`/`assignees` strings or
`{login:…}` objects; extra fields are ignored). CSV is the
equivalent columns. `closed` issues are skipped unless
`--include-done` (created `done` + archived).

## After importing

```sh
myco status         # the ledger, now bigger
myco board          # or the kanban view
myco check          # sanity
```

Each absorb run is one commit — `--no-commit` batches several
imports into one `myco commit`.

url: /myco/how-to/org-views.md
---
# See work across repos

`myco index` registers repos into a machine-wide cache;
`myco org` renders cross-repo views over it.

## The index

The index lives under `$MYCO_HOME`, else `$XDG_DATA_HOME/myco`,
else `~/.local/share/myco`:

* `repos.toml` — the registry (`[[repo]] path name`), a plain
  file you can inspect
* `index.redb` — one `snapshots` table: repo path → JSON snapshot

It is a **derived, disposable cache** — markdown in each repo's
`project/` stays canonical. `rm -rf` the index dir and
`myco index rebuild` derives it back.

## Register repos

```sh
myco index add ~/GitHub/9aia/sepia    # repo root or its project/ worktree
myco index add .                      # register the repo you're in
myco index list                       # repos + snapshot freshness
```

`add` takes an initial snapshot. Snapshots go stale as ledgers
change — `list` marks them `stale`; `org` verbs auto-rebuild
stale entries, or rebuild explicitly:

```sh
myco index rebuild                    # all registered repos
myco index rebuild ~/GitHub/9aia/sepia
myco index remove ~/GitHub/9aia/sepia # unregister + drop snapshot
```

## Org views

```sh
myco org status
```

```text
org status — 21 repo(s)
bupha            tasks 7o/0c/0ip/0b backlog 15 issues 0o p 0o pl 0o adr 2o  @ad8b625
sepia            tasks 2o/0c/0ip/0b backlog 4 issues 0o p 0o pl 1o adr 0o  @8cbc633
...
totals: tasks 167o/0c/1ip/0b backlog 326 issues 1o p 5o pl 7o/1r adr 59o
```

Per-repo counts (`o`pen / `c`laimed / `i`n-`p`rogress /
`b`locked), the snapshot commit, org totals, then items grouped
by owner. A rebuilt repo is marked `(rebuilt)`.

```sh
myco org board          # org kanban — repo-prefixed cards over every live item
myco org board --md     # markdown table for docs/READMEs
```

Cards are prefixed with the repo name (`thal:T-118 …`) so one
board spans the whole org.

## `myco`

myco — project management, grown not built: agent-first PM CLI

**Usage:** `myco [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `manifest` — Capabilities + protocol version — agent self-discovery
* `schema` — The file/state spec, machine-readable JSON Schema
* `init` — Scaffold `project/`: orphan branch + worktree + .gitignore + seed files. Idempotent — a valid existing worktree gets its scaffold verified/repaired
* `check` — Validate schemas + state machine, repair file/index drift. Exit 1 with findings; `--fix` applies safe repairs + commits
* `migrate` — Convert legacy ledgers to v2: `pm/` → `project/`, or normalize files already on the `project` branch
* `commit` — Stage + commit worktree changes (conventional message)
* `todo` — TODO.md tasks — add / done / defer / list
* `backlog` — BACKLOG.md parked items — add / promote / list
* `issue` — Tracked issues, one file each under `issues/`
* `proposal` — Design proposals under `proposals/` (`P-NNN`)
* `plan` — Execution plans under `plans/` (`PL-NNN`)
* `adr` — Architecture decision records under `adrs/` (`ADR-NNNN`)
* `item` — Kind-agnostic item verbs — show / set
* `handoff` — Attach resumable state at session end — appends a dated entry to `handoffs/<ID>.md` (any item kind, live or archived; append-only)
* `resume` — Minimal context block to restart work on an item — the item, `blocks:` dep titles, latest handoffs, open checklist. The single-item `status --prompt`
* `status` — Cheap digest of the work ledger. `--prompt` = token-sized
* `board` — Kanban of the ledger — Backlog | Open | Claimed | In Progress | Blocked. `--md` emits a markdown table
* `epic` — Items grouped by epic — bare lists epics with counts, a name renders that epic's board (`epic v2` ≡ `board --epic v2`)
* `milestone` — Items grouped by milestone — bare lists milestones with counts, a name renders that milestone's board
* `absorb` — Import work into the ledger — TODO/FIXME comments, Jira CSV exports, GitHub issue dumps
* `report` — Aging + velocity + blocked — how the ledger is trending
* `index` — The derived index: register repos, query/rebuild snapshots
* `org` — Cross-repo views over the index (auto-rebuilds stale repos)

###### **Options:**

* `--json` — Emit JSON (accepted everywhere; default output for machines)
* `--no-commit` — Skip the per-verb commit (also suppressed by $MYCO_NO_COMMIT)
* `--dir <PATH>` — Project worktree to act on, overriding discovery
* `--root <PATH>` — Repo root to act on, overriding discovery (the worktree is `<root>/project`)

## `myco manifest`

Capabilities + protocol version — agent self-discovery

**Usage:** `myco manifest`

## `myco schema`

The file/state spec, machine-readable JSON Schema

**Usage:** `myco schema`

## `myco init`

Scaffold `project/`: orphan branch + worktree + .gitignore + seed files. Idempotent — a valid existing worktree gets its scaffold verified/repaired

**Usage:** `myco init`

## `myco check`

Validate schemas + state machine, repair file/index drift. Exit 1 with findings; `--fix` applies safe repairs + commits

**Usage:** `myco check [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--fix` — Repair drift in place instead of only reporting

## `myco migrate`

Convert legacy ledgers to v2: `pm/` → `project/`, or normalize files already on the `project` branch

**Usage:** `myco migrate`

## `myco commit`

Stage + commit worktree changes (conventional message)

**Usage:** `myco commit [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `-m`, `--message <MESSAGE>` — Commit message (default: `chore: update project ledger`)

## `myco todo`

TODO.md tasks — add / done / defer / list

**Usage:** `myco todo <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `add` — Add a task — allocs a T-id, appends to a section of TODO.md
* `done` — Mark done — walks the state machine to `done`, then removes the line (git history keeps the record). Done on a parent removes the whole subtree — children die with it
* `defer` — Park a task — transition to `deferred`, move the line to BACKLOG.md. Defer on a parent moves the whole subtree (children park with it); on a child it detaches alone
* `list` — List tasks

## `myco todo add`

Add a task — allocs a T-id, appends to a section of TODO.md

**Usage:** `myco todo add [OPTIONS] <TITLE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<TITLE>` — One-line title

###### **Options:**

* `--section <SECTION>` — Section to add under (created when absent; default: the first section, or an unsectioned run)
* `--parent <PARENT>` — Nest under this task instead of a section — the new item becomes a child (`  - [ ]` under the parent)
* `--pri <PRI>` \[alias: `priority`] — Priority: low|med|high|crit
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Owner actor id (`devin`, `human:luis`, …)
* `--label <LABEL>` — `#label` — repeatable
* `--blocks <BLOCKS>` — Ids this item blocks — comma-separated or repeatable
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Epic name — the delivery grouping this item belongs to (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`)
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Milestone name — the target this item ships under (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`)

## `myco todo done`

Mark done — walks the state machine to `done`, then removes the line (git history keeps the record). Done on a parent removes the whole subtree — children die with it

**Usage:** `myco todo done <ID>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Task id (`T-NNN`)

## `myco todo defer`

Park a task — transition to `deferred`, move the line to BACKLOG.md. Defer on a parent moves the whole subtree (children park with it); on a child it detaches alone

**Usage:** `myco todo defer <ID>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Task id (`T-NNN`)

## `myco todo list`

List tasks

**Usage:** `myco todo list [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--status <STATUS>` — Keep only items with this status
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Keep only items owned by this actor
* `--label <LABEL>` — Keep only items carrying all of these labels (repeatable)

## `myco backlog`

BACKLOG.md parked items — add / promote / list

**Usage:** `myco backlog <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `add` — Add a deferred item — allocs a T-id straight into BACKLOG.md
* `promote` — Re-activate a parked item — `deferred → open`, move the line to TODO.md
* `list` — List backlog items

## `myco backlog add`

Add a deferred item — allocs a T-id straight into BACKLOG.md

**Usage:** `myco backlog add [OPTIONS] <TITLE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<TITLE>` — One-line title

###### **Options:**

* `--section <SECTION>` — Section to add under (created when absent; default: the first section, or an unsectioned run)
* `--pri <PRI>` \[alias: `priority`] — Priority: low|med|high|crit
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Owner actor id (`devin`, `human:luis`, …)
* `--label <LABEL>` — `#label` — repeatable
* `--blocks <BLOCKS>` — Ids this item blocks — comma-separated or repeatable
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Epic name — the delivery grouping this item belongs to (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`)
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Milestone name — the target this item ships under (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`)

## `myco backlog promote`

Re-activate a parked item — `deferred → open`, move the line to TODO.md

**Usage:** `myco backlog promote <ID>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Task id (`T-NNN`)

## `myco backlog list`

List backlog items

**Usage:** `myco backlog list [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--status <STATUS>` — Keep only items with this status
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Keep only items owned by this actor
* `--label <LABEL>` — Keep only items carrying all of these labels (repeatable)

# Config — `myco.toml`

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_dir` | `string` | optional | Path to the project worktree, relative to the repo root. |

## Constraints

* `deny_unknown_fields`: typos in field names fail the load.
* Search order: `$MYCO_CONFIG` → `./myco.toml` →
  `~/.config/myco/myco.toml`. The file is optional — no
  `myco.toml` anywhere just means defaults.

# The worktree model

Why `project/` is a git worktree of an orphan branch — and what
that buys you.

## The shape

```text
your-repo/
├── src/ …            ← code branch (main)
├── project/          ← worktree of the orphan `project` branch
│   ├── TODO.md
│   ├── BACKLOG.md
│   ├── issues/  proposals/  plans/  adrs/  handoffs/
│   ├── index.md
│   └── meta.toml
└── .gitignore        ← gains `project/`
```

The `project` branch shares the repo's `.git` object store but
has disjoint history — an orphan root, no code ancestors. The
worktree mounts it as a plain directory, so tools see ordinary
files while `git worktree list` shows the truth.

## Why an orphan branch

PM state moves at its own cadence. On an orphan branch, ledger
commits never touch the code history: no `chore: defer T-009`
noise in `main`'s log, no PM diffs in PRs, no branch protection
friction. `project/` is gitignored on every code branch — the
worktree physically can't leak into a code commit.

## Why a worktree (not just a branch)

The ledger has to be *visible* — agents edit files, humans read
`TODO.md` — without `git checkout` swapping the code tree. A
worktree keeps both checked out at once.

## Commits are the audit trail

Every mutating verb is one atomic, conventional commit on
`project` (`chore: add T-012`, `chore: handoff T-012`,
`chore: resolve I-003`, …). So
`git -C project log` *is* the history of intent — who moved what
when, replayable and greppable, with no separate audit store.
`--no-commit` / `$MYCO_NO_COMMIT` opts out per run; `myco commit`
squashes a batch into one.

## Canonical markdown, disposable index

The markdown in `project/` is canonical — human-editable,
diffable, frozen by golden fixtures. The redb index
(`index.redb` + `repos.toml` under `$MYCO_HOME` →
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/myco` → `~/.local/share/myco`) is a *derived
cache* that powers `status`, `board`, `report`, and `org` without
re-parsing files. Delete it and `myco index rebuild` derives it
back; `myco check` finds and repairs drift between the two.

See [the file spec](file-spec.md) for what the files contain and
[architecture](architecture.md) for the crates that implement it.

---

---
url: /myco/explanation/file-spec.md
---
# The ledger file spec

What `project/` contains, how items are written, and the state
machine they live under. `myco schema` emits all of this as
machine-readable JSON Schema; `myco check` enforces it.

## Layout

| path | holds |
|---|---|
| `meta.toml` | `name` + `[next]` per-kind id counters (`t`, `i`, `p`, `adr`, `pl`) |
| `TODO.md` | open-line tasks (`T-`), `##` sections, nested children |
| `BACKLOG.md` | deferred items — same grammar, no checkbox |
| `index.md` | free-form human index — verbatim, never rewritten |
| `issues/` | `issue-NNNN-<slug>.md` + `issues/archive/` |
| `proposals/` | `proposal-NNNN-<slug>.md` + `proposals/archive/` |
| `plans/` | `pl-NNNN-<slug>.md` + `plans/archive/` |
| `adrs/` | `NNNN-<slug>.md` + `adrs/archive/` |
| `handoffs/` | `<ID>.md` append-only + `handoffs/archive/` |

## Item ids

`<prefix>-<number>`, zero-padded per kind: `T-001` tasks,
`I-001` issues, `P-001` proposals, `PL-001` plans, `ADR-0001`
ADRs. One registry, per-kind counters in `meta.toml`'s `[next]`
table — ids are never reused. Tasks live as lines; the four
file-backed kinds (`I`, `P`, `PL`, `ADR`) get a markdown file
each, filenames padded to four digits.

## Line items — TODO.md / BACKLOG.md

```markdown
# TODO — <repo>

## <section>

- [ ] T-012 <title> · status:in-progress · pri:high · owner:devin · created:2026-10-29 · #label · blocks:I-001 · epic:v2 · ms:1.0 · note:<text>
  - [ ] T-013 a sub-task — children are the same grammar, indented 2 spaces/level
```

* `BACKLOG.md` lines are the same shape minus `[ ]`, default
  status `deferred`; `TODO.md` defaults to `open`.
* `done` removes the line (history keeps it); `defer` moves it to
  `BACKLOG.md`; `promote` moves it back.
* `done`/`defer` on a parent act on the whole subtree; on a
  child, just that node.
* Token order is canonical (`status`, `pri`, `owner`, `created`,
  `#label`, `blocks`, `epic`, `ms`, `note`) so emit produces
  minimal diffs. `ms` is the milestone token — kept short.
* Patterns: actors `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`, labels `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`,
  epic/ms names `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`, priority `low|med|high|crit`.

## File items — issues/ proposals/ plans/ adrs/

`+++` TOML frontmatter + free-form markdown body:

```markdown
+++
id = "P-001"
title = "myco v2 — agent-first project management, in Rust"
status = "open"
created = "2026-10-29"
priority = "medium"
labels = ["design"]
blocks = ["T-008"]
epic = "v2"
milestone = "1.0"
+++

# Title

Body — templates seed Context/Decision/Consequences-shaped
sections per kind.
```

Frontmatter keys: `id`, `title`, `status`, `created`, `owner`,
`priority`, `labels`, `blocks`, `note`, `superseded_by`,
`supersedes`, `epic`, `milestone`. Archiving moves the file to
`<dir>/archive/` — `myco item show` still finds archived items.

## State machine

Six statuses; `item set --status` and kind verbs walk it one
legal step at a time:

| from | can go to |
|---|---|
| `open` | `claimed`, `in-progress`, `deferred` |
| `claimed` | `in-progress`, `open`, `deferred` |
| `in-progress` | `blocked`, `done`, `deferred` |
| `blocked` | `in-progress`, `open`, `deferred` |
| `deferred` | `open` |
| `done` | — (terminal) |

Proposal words alias the machine: `draft` = `open`, `accepted` =
`done`, `rejected` = `deferred` — the transition still walks the
graph (`accepted` passes `open → in-progress → done`). ADR status
`open` reads as "proposed"; `adr supersede` closes the old file
with `superseded_by:` and stamps the replacement `supersedes:`.

## Handoffs

`handoffs/<ID>.md` — one file per item, uniform across kinds:

```markdown
+++
item = "T-012"
+++

# Handoffs — T-012

## 2026-10-29 · devin · session:cli:abc123
Done: parser. Next: emitter. Open: archive semantics.
```

Append-only: every `myco handoff` is one `##` entry + one commit;
entries are never rewritten. When an item's file goes away, its
handoff file is orphaned — `myco check` reports it and
`check --fix` moves it to `handoffs/archive/`, where `resume`
still finds it.

---

---
url: /myco/explanation/architecture.md
---
# Architecture

Ports-and-adapters over a flat `crates/` workspace:
`myco-core` is pure domain — item models, the id registry, the
state machine — with no I/O. Ports are traits (`myco-store`,
`myco-config`, `myco-index`); impls live in separate crates;
`crates/myco-cli` (package `myco`) is the composition root that
wires impls to verbs.

Design rules:

* **No `unsafe`, no async** — the binary stays dependency-light
  and synchronous; no runtime to embed.
* **Git via the `git` CLI** — `myco-git` shells out for the
  orphan branch, worktree, and per-verb commits; no
  libgit2/gix binding.
* **Markdown is the file spec** — `myco-store-md` owns strict
  parse/emit: deterministic output, stable ordering, minimal
  diffs. `myco-testkit` freezes emit with golden fixtures and
  proptest round-trips, so the format can't drift silently.
* **The index is derived, never canonical** — `myco-index-redb`
  snapshots ledgers into redb for `status`/`board`/`org`; it can
  be deleted and rebuilt at any time.

| crate | layer | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `myco-core` | domain | myco domain core: item models, ID registry, state machine — pure, no I/O |
| `myco-config` | port | Config port: where myco.toml-shaped config comes from |
| `myco-index` | port | Index port: the derived, disposable cache powering status/board/report/org views |
| `myco-store` | port | Store port: where project/ state (TODO.md, BACKLOG.md, meta.toml, item files) is persisted |
| `myco-config-toml` | adapter | Config impl: myco.toml file (explicit path, env, ./, ~/.config) |
| `myco-git` | adapter | Git plumbing for myco — shells out to the git CLI; owns the project branch/worktree mechanics |
| `myco-index-redb` | adapter | Index impl: redb snapshots + repos.toml registry under ~/.local/share/myco (disposable derived cache) |
| `myco-shell` | adapter | Run a command in a working directory via bash -c — the generic shell-out helper |
| `myco-store-md` | adapter | Markdown adapter for the store port — strict parse/emit of project/ files, round-trip stable; owns the file spec |
| `myco-testkit` | adapter | Golden fixtures + conformance: frozen md emit snapshots and proptest round-trips for the project/ file spec |
| `myco` | binary | myco — project management, grown not built: agent-first PM CLI |

## Boundary — work memory only

myco owns the ledger of intent (tasks, issues, proposals, plans,
ADRs, handoffs). Neighbors own their own memory:

* **sturn** — ephemeral coordination (live claims/ops/topics)
* **kuda** — code memory; myco indexes work items, not code
* **peregrin** — orchestration; an optional `myco serve` ndjson
  wire is deferred per `adrs/0001`
* **bupha** — CI gate; `myco check` in pipelines, `Item:` trailers
* **mycena** — surfaces TODO/FIXME in code → `myco absorb`
* **sepia** — session lifecycle → `myco handoff` / `myco resume`

Anything needing a daemon, a multi-machine view, or arbitration
between actors belongs to peregrin, not here.

---

---
url: /myco/explanation/release-model.md
---
# Release model

Releases are repo automation, not manual steps:
`scripts/release.sh` is triggered by bupha watch on each `main`
push — a debounce window (default 5 min, `MYCO_RELEASE_DEBOUNCE`)
means only the last push in a quiet window actually releases. The
script runs inside a detached worktree and pushes commits and
tags from there, never from the main checkout.

## What a release run does

1. **Diff since the last tag** — crates under `crates/` that
   changed since `git describe --tags` are the release set; the
   `myco` binary re-publishes whenever any crate changed. No
   crate changes, no release.
2. **Per-crate patch bump + publish** —
   `cargo set-version -p <crate> --bump patch`, then
   `cargo publish` with retries.
   Each crate gets its own tag `<crate>-v<ver>` — versions
   diverge independently in the monorepo.
3. **Commit + push** — one `release: bump crate versions` commit,
   pushed to `main` with the tags.
4. **Binary dist** — when `dist` and `gh` are available, a local
   `dist build` produces the shell installer
   (`dist-workspace.toml`, host arch `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
   only — other targets are a TODO for remote workers), uploaded
   to a GitHub Release `myco-v<ver>` with generated notes.

With no tags at all the script exits early — the flow is seeded
by tagging once.

## Constraints

* The crates.io name `myco` is currently held by an unrelated
  project, so `cargo publish` of the CLI package depends on
  resolving that; installs should use
  `cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/myco` regardless.
* Library crates publish normally under their `myco-*` names.

## CI and docs deploys

The same bupha watch owns the rest of what used to be GitHub
Actions — there are no workflows in the repo:

* **Push to `docs`** runs `scripts/deploy-docs.sh`, which
  rebuilds the site and pushes `gh-pages` — Pages is a legacy
  branch deploy, so that push is the whole release of the site.
* **Push to `main`** is gated locally by the `pre-push` hook
  (`cargo xtask check`). `scripts/ci.sh` (`check && test`) is
  ready for bupha, but the watcher routes one `branch` per repo
  name today — a second `9aia/myco` entry needs bupha's
  `[[repo.jobs]]` work (its T-004).

---

---
url: /myco/getting-started.md
---
# Getting started

Install the `myco` CLI, then turn a repo's `project/` directory
into a work ledger — tasks, issues, proposals, plans, ADRs,
handoffs — that lives on its own orphan branch.

## Install

The crates.io name `myco` belongs to an unrelated project —
install from the repo:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/myco
```

From a checkout of this repo: `cargo xtask install` builds and
installs the release binary to `~/.cargo/bin/myco`.

## Set up a repo

```sh
cd your-repo
myco init
```

`init` creates the orphan `project` branch, mounts it as a
`project/` worktree, seeds `meta.toml`, `TODO.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
`index.md` and the item dirs (`issues/`, `proposals/`, `plans/`,
`adrs/`, `handoffs/`), and adds `project/` to `.gitignore` on your
code branch. It is idempotent — run it again and a healthy
worktree is verified, a damaged one repaired.

## First items

```sh
myco todo add "ship the thing" --pri high --label release
myco item set T-001 --status in-progress
myco status            # ledger digest
myco todo done T-001   # the line leaves TODO.md — git history keeps it
```

Every mutating verb is one atomic commit on the `project` branch —
the branch history is the audit trail. `--no-commit` (or the
`MYCO_NO_COMMIT` env var) opts out.

## Agent self-discovery

```sh
myco manifest          # capabilities + protocol version (JSON)
myco schema            # the file/state spec as JSON Schema
myco status --prompt   # token-sized digest for a context window
```

Every verb accepts `--json`. `myco check` validates the ledger —
file schemas, state machine, index drift — and `myco check --fix`
repairs what it safely can.

## Where next

* [Your first item](tutorials/first-item.md) — a guided walk
  through a full task lifecycle.
* [Set up myco on a repository](how-to/init-repo.md) — discovery,
  overrides, non-standard layouts.
* [The worktree model](explanation/worktree-model.md) — what is
  actually on disk and why.
* [CLI reference](reference/cli.md) — the full verb surface.
